english: intend to V / plan to V
formNote: Add 려고 after a vowel stem and 으려고 after a consonant stem, then 해요. It shows your own plan or intention.
examples: I plan to sleep early tomorrow.
I intend to meet a friend this weekend.
I plan to learn Korean this year.
mistakes: Use this for your own plan, not another person.

formNote: Make the 아/어 form first, then add 주시겠어요. It is more polite than 주세요 and good for asking strangers or staff.
usage: Could you please say it again?
examples: Could you please help me with this?
Could you please open the window?
mistakes: More polite than 주세요. Use it with strangers.

english: it is good to V / you should V
formNote: Attach 는 게 좋아요 to a plain verb stem to give gentle advice. ㄹ stems drop the ㄹ, so 만들다 becomes 만드는 게 좋아요.
usage: It is good to sleep early.
examples: If you are tired, you should rest.
감기에는 물을 많이 마시는 게 좋아요.
For a cold you should drink lots of water.
시험 전에는 일찍 자는 게 좋아요.
Before a test it is good to sleep early.
mistakes: 게 is short for 것이. Keep it as 는 게.

english: I think it will / it seems
formNote: Add ㄹ 것 같아요 after a vowel stem and 을 것 같아요 after a consonant stem to make a soft guess about the future.
usage: I think I will be late.
It looks like it will be tasty.
I think it will be good.
examples: 오늘 오후에 비가 올 것 같아요.
I think it will rain this afternoon.
길이 막혀서 좀 늦을 것 같아요.
The road is busy, so I will be a bit late.
I think this movie will be fun.
mistakes: This is a soft guess, not a sure fact.

formNote: Add ㄴ 적이 있어요 after a vowel stem and 은 적이 있어요 after a consonant stem to talk about a past experience. Use 없어요 for the negative.
examples: 저는 제주도에 가 본 적이 있어요.
I have been to Jeju Island before.
I have watched a Korean movie before.
mistakes: For never, use 없어요. Say 간 적이 없어요.

formNote: Put a noun before 때문에 to give the cause or reason. No particle goes between the noun and 때문에.
examples: I canceled the plan because of the rain.
I am very busy because of work.
I could not go to school because of a cold.
mistakes: No particle before 때문에. Say 비 때문에.

english: because / since V (reason for a request)
formNote: Add 니까 after a vowel stem and 으니까 after a consonant stem. Use it to give a reason before a request or suggestion.
examples: Since it is raining, please take an umbrella.
Since I am busy today, let us meet tomorrow.
Since this place is tasty, let us eat here.
mistakes: Use 니까, not 아서, before requests and suggestions.

formNote: Attach 처럼 directly to a noun to say something is similar to it. No particle goes between the noun and 처럼.
examples: That person sings well like a singer.
Today the weather is warm like spring.
I want to speak like a Korean person too.
mistakes: 처럼 means similar to, not more than like 보다.

english: even if V / even though V
formNote: Make the 아/어 form first, then add 도 to mean even if. Use 아 after ㅏ or ㅗ, otherwise 어, and 해 for 하다 verbs.
examples: Even if it rains, I will go.
Even if I am busy, I exercise every day.
Even if it is a bit expensive, I will buy this.
mistakes: Pick the right vowel. Say 와도, not 오아도.

english: while doing V (at the same time)
formNote: Add 면서 after a vowel stem and 으면서 after a consonant stem. The same person does both actions at the same time.
examples: I study while listening to music.
I talk with a friend while drinking coffee.
mistakes: One person does both actions, not two people.
